text:
MacKenzie Weegar is a seventh-round success story: 206th overall in 2013, through the ECHL and AHL, and now past 600 NHL games. With Utah he is logging 22 minutes a night and doing the heavy lifting: 57 hits and 50 blocked shots in 18 games. The Ottawa Citizen's latest piece on the Ottawa native: he "thought about being an Ottawa Senator, but the Utah Mammoth feels like home."

The points haven't come, and that's the misleading part. At five on five, Utah gets 59% of the expected goals (the quality of chances, for and against) with him on the ice. Yet the team has scored 11.7 fewer goals than those chances deserve while he's out there. That kind of gap usually swings back, and when it does, his five points should start to look more like his play.

Last season was rough by Evolving-Hockey's numbers, around replacement level, though their expected version (built from chance quality) rated him better than his results, and penalties cost him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking credits him with clean breakouts: 49% of his exits leave the zone with the puck. Our range has him finishing with 21 to 37 points.
headline: MacKenzie Weegar is playing well. Utah isn't scoring.
